knowledge_point.title: Finding the Jacobian of an Inverse Transformation

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w))$, given that

$$u=- 4 x\qquad v=y\qquad w=z.$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation

$$T:(u,v,w)\to(x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T$ is $\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}$.

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}$, the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$.

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1}.$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=-4 & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=0 & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z}=0 \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=0 & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y}=1 & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z}=0 \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x}=0 & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y}=0 & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}=1\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}&=|\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial u}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial u}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial v}{\partial z} \\ \frac{\partial w}{\partial x} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial y} & \frac{\partial w}{\partial z}\end{aligned}| \\ &=|\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ &=-4|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\ &=-4\left(1\cdot 1-0\right) \\ &=-4\end{aligned}$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$\begin{aligned}\frac{\partial(x,y,z)}{\partial(u,v,w)}&=\left(\frac{\partial(u,v,w)}{\partial(x,y,z)}\right)^{-1} \\ &=- \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}$$

generation.domain: x,y,z real; nonzero constant inverse determinant

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),$ given that 

$$
u=2\left(z-y\right),\,v=2\left(x+z\right),\,w=4\left(-3x\right).
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =2\left(-1\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =2\left(1\right) \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =2\left(1\right) & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =2\left(1\right) \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =4\left(-3\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Scaling the three derivative rows by $2, 2, 4$ multiplies the determinant by $16$.

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2\left(-1\right) & 2\left(1\right) \\ 2\left(1\right) & 0 & 2\left(1\right) \\ 4\left(-3\right) & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =16\left(-(-1)|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -3 & 0\end{aligned}|\right)\\  & =16\left(1(0+3)+1(0-0)\right)\\  & =48\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{48}\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: x,y,z real; nonzero constant inverse determinant

question.:question/problem:
Find the Jacobian determinant of the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)),$ given that 

$$
u=4\left(3x+yz\right),\,v=z,\,w=4\left(-y\right).
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =4\left(3\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =4\left(z\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =4\left(y\right) \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =1 \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =4\left(-1\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Scaling the three derivative rows by $4, 1, 4$ multiplies the determinant by $16$.

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4\left(3\right) & 4\left(z\right) & 4\left(y\right) \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 4\left(-1\right) & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =16\left(3|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}|\right)\\  & =16\left(3(0+1)\right)\\  & =48\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{48}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)).$ The inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}(x,y,z)\to (u(x,y,z),v(x,y,z),w(x,y,z))$ is given by

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2\left(x\right) \\ 2\left(z-y\right) \\ 4\left(xy\right)\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the Jacobian determinant of $T.$

*Hint: You can assume that $x\ne 0.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

Here, we have 

$$
u(x,y,z)=2\left(x\right),\,v(x,y,z)=2\left(z-y\right),\,w(x,y,z)=4\left(xy\right).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =2\left(1\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =0 \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =2\left(-1\right) & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & =2\left(1\right) \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =4\left(y\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =4\left(x\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Scaling the three derivative rows by $2, 2, 4$ multiplies the determinant by $16$.

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2\left(1\right) & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\left(-1\right) & 2\left(1\right) \\ 4\left(y\right) & 4\left(x\right) & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =16\left(1|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ x & 0\end{aligned}|\right)\\  & =16\left(1(0-x)\right)\\  & =- 16 x.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing down $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)}$ in terms of $u,$ $v,$ and $w,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}16\left(-x\right) & =16\left(-\left(\frac{u}{2}\right)\right)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}\left(\frac{1}{(-\left(\frac{u}{2}\right))}\right) \\  & =- \frac{1}{8 u}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the transformation $T:(u,v,w)\to (x(u,v,w),y(u,v,w),z(u,v,w)).$ The inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}(x,y,z)\to (u(x,y,z),v(x,y,z),w(x,y,z))$ is given by

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}4\left(y{z}^{2}\right) \\ z{x}^{2} \\ 4\left(x{y}^{2}\right)\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the Jacobian determinant of $T.$

*Hint: You can assume that $x,y,z>0.$*
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v \\ w\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v,w) \\ y(u,v,w) \\ z(u,v,w)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} & \frac{∂x}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v} & \frac{∂y}{∂w} \\ \frac{∂z}{∂u} & \frac{∂z}{∂v} & \frac{∂z}{∂w}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)}={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1}.
$$

Here, we have 

$$
u(x,y,z)=4\left(y{z}^{2}\right),\,v(x,y,z)=z{x}^{2},\,w(x,y,z)=4\left(x{y}^{2}\right).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =0 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =4\left({z}^{2}\right) & \,\frac{∂u}{∂z} & =4\left(2yz\right) \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =2xz & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =0 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂z} & ={x}^{2} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & =4\left({y}^{2}\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂y} & =4\left(2xy\right) & \,\frac{∂w}{∂z} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Scaling the three derivative rows by $4, 1, 4$ multiplies the determinant by $16$.

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} & \frac{∂u}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y} & \frac{∂v}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂w}{∂x} & \frac{∂w}{∂y} & \frac{∂w}{∂z}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 4\left({z}^{2}\right) & 4\left(2yz\right) \\ 2xz & 0 & {x}^{2} \\ 4\left({y}^{2}\right) & 4\left(2xy\right) & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =16\left(-{z}^{2}|\begin{aligned}2xz & {x}^{2} \\ {y}^{2} & 0\end{aligned}|+2yz|\begin{aligned}2xz & 0 \\ {y}^{2} & 2xy\end{aligned}|\right)\\  & =16\left(-{z}^{2}(0-{x}^{2}{y}^{2})+2yz(4{x}^{2}yz-0)\right)\\  & =16\left({x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}+8{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\right)\\  & =144 x^{2} y^{2} z^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Writing down $\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)}$ in terms of $u,$ $v,$ and $w,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}16\left(9{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\right) & =16\left(9{({x}^{3}{y}^{3}{z}^{3})}^{2/3}\right) \\  & =16\left(9{(y{z}^{2}\cdot z{x}^{2}\cdot x{y}^{2})}^{2/3}\right) \\  & =16\left(9(\left(\frac{u}{4}\right)v\left(\frac{w}{4}\right))^{2/3}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y,z)}{∂(u,v,w)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v,w)}{∂(x,y,z)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{2^{\frac{2}{3}}}{36 \left(u v w\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$
